Syllabus (GS3): Money & Banking - barter, money, coins, digital payments, crypto, CBDC.

1. Money: Meaning, Functions & Evolution

Q - What was the Barter system and why did it fail?

Barter = direct exchange of goods for goods (Mesopotamian tribes). It failed due to:





Double coincidence of wants - both sides must want what the other has.



High search & transaction cost.



Perishables can't store value - value is lost over time.



No specialization / division of labour.

Layman: You grow tomatoes and want shoes -> you must find a shoemaker who also wants tomatoes. Clumsy, so money was invented.

Q - What are the functions of money?







Category



Functions





Primary



Measure of value; Medium of exchange





Secondary



Store of value; Transfer of value; Standard of deferred payments (EMI)





Contingent



Basis of financial market; Mobilises factors of production; Redistributes national income

Q - How did money evolve, and what are its types?

Evolution chain: Commodity -> Metallic -> Paper/Token/Fiat -> Bank (Deposit) -> Cryptocurrency.







Type (intrinsic value)



Key points & examples





Commodity money (Yes)



Iron nails, bear pelts, cocoa beans, whale teeth, gold nuggets. Problems: perishable, not uniform/pure, foreigners may reject.





Metallic money (Yes)



Kings stamped gold for trust. Indo-Greek & Kushana gold coins; Gupta coins most spectacular. Delhi Sultanate: Silver Tanka; Sher Shah Suri: Rupiya; Akbar: Muhr.





Paper / Fiat money (No)



Value by govt command ('fiat'); it is legal tender.





Bank / Deposit money (No)



Cheque, Demand Draft, digital transfers.





Cryptocurrency (No)



Decentralised, blockchain-based.

Q - Full-bodied vs Token coins?







Full-bodied coins



Token coins





Example: Gupta coin (~8 gm gold)



Example: 50 paise coin (~4 gm steel)





Intrinsic value >= face value



Intrinsic value < face value





Risk: Debasement (less metal when ruler weak - Aurangzeb, Roman kings)



Modern Indian coins are token coins; cupronickel discourages melting; Coinage Act 2011 bans melting

Intrinsic value: metal coins can be melted for jewellery/weapons (metal has use); paper notes have NO intrinsic value (paper alone is useless).

2. Fiat Money & Legal Tender

Q - What is Fiat money? (two conditions together)





It must be a physical coin/note OR a digital/crypto coin that can measure value; AND



It must be issued by order of a King/Queen/Government/Central Bank.







Issuer



What & how





Government (Coinage Act 2011)



All coins up to Rs.1,000 + the Rs.1 note. Rs.1 note is signed by the Finance Secretary and has NO 'I promise to pay'. Rs.20 coin = 12-sided dodecagon.





RBI (RBI Act 1934)



All currency notes except Rs.1; they carry the Governor's sign and 'I promise to pay the bearer...'.

Q - What is Legal Tender? (two conditions together)





It must be fiat money; AND



It must be legally valid for all debts/transactions country-wide (other party cannot refuse).

Fiat money vs legal tender - quick check:





Rupee coins/notes & CBDC (e-Rs): fiat = yes, legal tender = yes.



Old demonetized Rs.500/1000, foreign currency (USD/Yuan/Euro): fiat = yes, legal tender = no.



G-Sec, T-Bill: fiat = no, legal tender = no.



Shares, bonds, DD, cheque, cards: fiat = no, legal tender = no.



Bitcoin: fiat = no, legal tender = no (exception: El Salvador).



Commemorative coins: fiat = yes but NOT legal tender unless notified by RBI/Govt.

Q - Limited vs Unlimited legal tender?







Limited legal tender



Unlimited legal tender





Recipient can refuse beyond a limit (Coinage Act 2011)



No such limit (RBI Act 1934, Sec 26)





Coins Rs.1+ up to Rs.1000; 50 paise coins up to Rs.10



Every bank note. (The Rs.1 paper note is LIMITED legal tender.)





Below 50 paise withdrawn (2011): 10p, 25p are NOT legal tender; 50 paise IS



Note: Finance Act 2017 caps cash transactions below Rs.2 lakh (anti-black-money)

3. Currency GK, Demonetization & Rs.2000





MANI App (2020): 'Mobile Aided Note Identifier' by RBI helps the blind identify notes (camera + audio in Hindi/English, offline, vibrations for deaf-blind); CANNOT detect fake notes.



Rupee symbol: chosen via a Dept of Economic Affairs competition (2010); designed by D. Udaya Kumar (IIT Guwahati).



National emblem: Lion Capital from Sarnath Pillar (UP); 'Satyamev Jayate' from Mundaka Upanishad.



Languages: 17 on a note (15 reverse + Hindi & English obverse); 8th Schedule has 22.



'I promise to pay': convertible into other notes/token coins of equal face value; not gold-linked, not inflation-adjusted; a note is a zero-interest anonymous bearer bond.

Q - Demonetization vs Rs.2000 withdrawal?

Demonetization = removal of legal-tender status (earlier 1946, 1978). 8-Nov-2016: FinMin/DEA banned Rs.500 & Rs.1000 (Mahatma Gandhi series); the Specified Bank Notes (Cessation of Liabilities) Act 2017 made holding them illegal (except research/museum).

Rs.2000 note: fiat money = YES, legal tender = YES, withdrawn from circulation (2023-May) = YES, but demonetized = NOT yet (as of 2025-Jan). Reasons for withdrawal: temporary post-demonetization measure, enough other notes, rarely used, RBI 'clean note policy' (4-5 yr paper life). No black-money/fake-note reason cited.

4. Bank Money - Cheque, DD, CTS





Law: Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 (Viceroy Ripon) - against cheque dishonour & forgery.



Cheque parties: Drawer (sender), Drawee (bank), Payee (recipient).



Cheque types: Stale (not deposited within 3 months), Post-dated, Open/bearer (no crossing).



IFSC: 11 alphanumeric code identifying a bank branch (like a PIN code).



MICR: 9-digit code in iron-oxide ink for automated clearing.



Overdraft: withdraw beyond balance (as a loan); short-term (PMJDY OD up to Rs.10,000). Loans = longer term.



CTS (Cheque Truncation System): sends scanned cheque image online - faster than courier.



Positive Pay: sender pre-confirms cheque details; if tampered, images mismatch -> cheque rejected.

CTS reforms: 2024 -> settlement in a few hours (T+1, settlement-on-realisation). The 2026-Jan 3-hour clearing plan was postponed.

5. Digital Payments - CBS, NEFT/RTGS/IMPS

Payment & Settlement Systems Act 2007 empowers RBI to regulate card/e-payments. CBS (Core Banking Solution) = centralized branch-less banking software (Finacle, BanCS, RBI's E-Kuber).

The three fund-transfer systems:





RTGS (RBI) - high-value, instant.





Amount: min Rs.2 lakh, no upper cap.



Settlement: instant (gross); Timing: 24/7; inward free, outward up to Rs.50 (SBI free).



NEFT (RBI) - retail/small amounts.





Amount: Rs.1 to ~Rs.25 lakh (bank-wise).



Settlement: net, every 30 min; Timing: 24/7; Rs.0 fees after RBI reform.



IMPS (NPCI) - retail, instant.





Amount: Rs.1 to Rs.5 lakh.



Settlement: instant; Timing: 24/7; small transactions usually free.

Since 2021, non-bank entities can also join RBI's centralized payment systems (NEFT/RTGS).





LPSS: RBI's bare-bones backup to NEFT/RTGS/UPI during war/disaster (minimum staff).



Beneficiary name look-up (2024): verify payee name from account no.+IFSC before sending (now NEFT/RTGS too) -> fewer frauds.

6. NPCI, UPI & BHIM

NPCI (2008): a 'Not-for-Profit Company' (Companies Act); founded by 10 banks (Rs.100 cr), later Paytm/PhonePe/Amazon Pay joined as shareholders (2020). Provides cost-effective payment tech; aids financial inclusion.

UPI = tech to build payment apps on IMPS: QR scan-and-pay, links a bank account directly (no wallet needed), supports Push (you send), Pull (auto-debit e.g. electricity) and bill-split.





Delegated payments (2024): primary holder creates a secondary account (father -> daughter) with a spending limit.



UPI Lite: on-device wallet, no UPI-PIN needed (faster, fewer failures); needs internet.



UPI Lite X: offline via NFC; sync online later.



Conversational payments: voice/AI payments; helps blind users.







UPI daily limit



Category





Rs.1 lakh



Normal transactions





Rs.2 lakh



Capital markets (MF), credit-card/loan/EMI/insurance payments





Rs.5 lakh



G-Sec (Retail Direct), IPO, medical & education fees, tax payment

Pre-sanctioned Credit Line in UPI (2023): borrow up to a pre-set limit without a fresh loan -> enables BNPL (Buy Now Pay Later); aids the poor. ICCW = card-less ATM withdrawal (less cloning). UPI can also deposit (CDM) & withdraw cash without a card.





BHIM (2016): 'Bharat Interface for Money' by NPCI; works on smart & basic phones (*99# USSD); money stays in bank (earns interest); no MDR.



BHIM 3.0 (2025): 15+ languages, slow-internet mode, bill-split, expense tracker.



BHIM Vega: pay inside a merchant app without switching to a 3rd-party app.



RuPay (2012): world's 7th card gateway (vs Visa/Mastercard/UnionPay); lower fees; free with PMJDY.



Other NPCI systems: BBPS (bills), NFS (ATM network), NETC (FASTag), DakPay, DigiSaathi (14431).

7. DBT / e-RUPI & QR Codes

e-RUPI (2021): SMS/QR-based prepaid cashless voucher by NPCI on UPI; backed by DFS & National Health Authority.





Who can buy (2023 expansion): Govt + private companies -> now individuals too (e.g. gift to maid/driver).



Who can sell: only banks -> now non-bank PPIs (AmazonPay etc.) too.



Max value: Rs.10,000 -> Rs.1 lakh.





Proprietary QR: Paytm/PhonePe exclusive, not interoperable -> RBI banned new ones.



UPI QR: by NPCI; scannable by all UPI apps.



Bharat QR: by NPCI + Visa/Mastercard; interoperable. rMQR = rectangular micro QR for narrow spaces.

8. Cards, MDR & ATMs





Credit card: shopping on credit; ATM withdrawal = borrowing (interest).



Debit card: uses own balance; ATM withdrawal is not borrowing.



Hybrid/Duo card: two chips (credit + debit) in one (e.g. IndusInd).



Prepaid card: debit sub-type bought without a bank account (e.g. IRCTC-UBI RuPay prepaid).



Tokenization (2022): replaces card data with a 'token' so the merchant never sees real card no.



Additional authentication (from Apr-2026): risk-based beyond OTP, for both international AND domestic suspicious transactions.



Network portability (2024) & CVC-less: customer can pick card network; CVC not always needed.



Transport: NCMC 'One Nation One Card' (2019, MoHUA+NPCI+BEL; SWEEKAR fare + SWAGAT gate); FASTag/NETC (2017, RFID, mandatory 2021).

MDR (Merchant Discount Rate): fee a merchant pays his acquirer bank per card transaction (shared among issuing bank, acquiring bank, gateway); hurts margins, so RBI capped it (2017).







Instrument



MDR on transaction





UPI



0%





RuPay Debit card



0%





RuPay Credit card / Visa / Mastercard



'x'% (not zero)

Govt gives a 0.15% incentive to small merchants on UPI up to Rs.2,000. 2025-Aug: FinMin confirms NO user fees on UPI.





ATM types: Bank label (bank owns+runs), Brown label (bank owns, ops outsourced), White label (non-bank e.g. Muthoot/Tata), Micro-ATM (bank-mitra + Aadhaar biometrics via AePS).



PIDF: Rs.500 cr fund (Rs.250 RBI + Rs.250 banks) to subsidise PoS machines in small towns/villages/NE (2021).

9. Global Money Transfer & SWIFT





Foreign tourists (2023): NRE/NRO/FCNR account holders can use UPI in India.



RuPay international (2023): usable abroad (Mauritius 2024).



UPI abroad: Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, UAE, Singapore, France, Mauritius etc. (formal UPI deal: UAE, France, Singapore).



India-UAE LCSS (2023): Local Currency Settlement System - trade in INR & AED (no dollar); UPI-IPP linkage.



JAYWAN & AANI (UAE): JAYWAN = RuPay-based card; AANI = UPI-like; built on NPCI's model.



Project Nexus (2024): links India UPI with Malaysia/Philippines/Singapore/Thailand FPS; coordinator = BIS (Basel).



EU-TIPS (2025): UPI linkage with EU's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement.







SWIFT (global)



SFMS (within India)





Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication



Structured Financial Messaging System





Belgium cooperative (1973)



Built by TCS for IDRBT (RBI's research arm)





Banned: Iran; Russia (2022, post-Ukraine)

10. Digital Payment Regulators

Digital Transactions Ombudsman (2019): senior RBI officials at 21 places; hear complaints up to Rs.20 lakh; can order a fix + up to Rs.1 lakh for mental agony; appeal to Dy. Governor; above Rs.20 lakh -> courts.

Q - BPSS replaced by PRB (2025)?

11. Cryptocurrency & Blockchain

Cryptocurrency = digital currency created/stored using blockchain. Blockchain = decentralized distributed-ledger database (old entries can't be deleted). Origin: distrust of fiat after the 2007 US subprime crisis; 2009 Satoshi Nakamoto launched Bitcoin (max 21 million; 1 BTC = 10^8 Satoshi).





Meme coin: named after celebrities/animals/art by private coders - Dogecoin (2013, first), $TRUMP (2025).



Hot vs Cold wallet: Hot = online (app); Cold = offline (USB pendrive).



Prices: 2021-22 'Crypto Winter' ($70k->$20k); 2024-Dec $100k; 2026-Jan fell to $87,500.



US Bitcoin Strategic Reserve (2025): from ~200,000 seized bitcoins (like the 1975 Strategic Petroleum Reserve).



Scams: Binance, FTX (CEO arrested), WazirX ($230M+ hack 2024), CoinDCX ($44M 2025).



EcoSurvey 2023 concerns: 'whales' manipulate prices, electricity use, tax evasion, fraud, no intrinsic value.

Stablecoin: crypto backed by a reserve asset (gold/dollar) e.g. Tether, TrueUSD, Libra.

13. Fungibility & NFT

Fungible = subdivisible AND mutually substitutable in value (Rs.500 note, gold bar, Bitcoin). Non-fungible = a big single diamond, shares/bonds, NFT.

NFT = a unique digital file (JPEG/GIF/MP3) or ownership document on blockchain; cannot be subdivided (e.g. Beeple's $70M JPEG). Charms: easy trade, verify ownership, paperless tickets. Challenges: price bubble, money laundering, electricity/CO2. RBI: programmability does not destroy the rupee's fungibility.
